title: meta: with two package holders of one dashboard name, GET /meta/dashboard/X/layers silently returns one holder's overlay while package-less save and delete answer 409
body:
domain:devx#2 · os-justin · session_01QSeKYmTYfaPbLQD4BJfomW

Filing gate: ① an observed, reproduced inconsistency from the 18.3.0 release-candidate run. W3-C2b, record #27438, at `c4c515ad`, parked on the wave anchor #27377 as a **ruling** finding. Item: `platform-core.metadata-registry-serving`. ⛔ Not a claim; triage grades and routes. Suggested labels are suggestions only.

## Observed
The record (W3-C2b comment 6494110310 on #27377) reads, verbatim:

> with two package holders, `GET /meta/dashboard/X/layers` silently returns one holder's overlay, while the package-less save and delete on that name answer 409.

When two packages both hold a dashboard of the same name:
- the read door (`/layers`) picks one holder **silently**;
- the write doors (a save or delete without `?package=`) **refuse** with 409, because the name is ambiguous.

One name gives two answers to the same ambiguity. A reader of `/layers`, whether the Studio or an agent, cannot tell that a second holder exists, or which holder it got.

## Why it may matter
- **Who:** anyone who installs two packages that ship the same dashboard name, and the Studio or agent reading layers for it.
- **What happens:** the layer stack shown or edited belongs to whichever holder `/layers` picked, while a save on the same name is refused. This invites a wrong edit target or a confusing refusal.
- **Not measured:** how often two holders of one dashboard name occur in real installs, and which holder `/layers` picks (registration order?).

## Possible directions (for the owner and triage; not a recommendation)
- `/layers` refuses the same way the write doors do (409 plus the holders' package ids), or requires `?package=`;
- or `/layers` returns every holder's stack, keyed by package;
- or the current behaviour is ruled correct and documented, in which case the checklist item records it.

## Dedupe
- Read #20680 and #23165: related, closed, different. The census's semantic search found no open card.
